name: Python records check
scoped_purpose: Use for checking a repository's intent records (problems, ideals, solutions, implementations, metrics) against the intent template: every required field filled, links resolving both ways, parent links resolving in the overall network. Avoids judging whether an intent is worth having.
goals: A defect in a record is reported with its rule and its id; a complete network is never flagged.
knowledge: The parsed intent template shipped with the package; the shape of the five record files.
measures_of_success: Every injected defect is reported by the right rule and a complete network passes.
parameters: Whether interface fields are required, whether a command is required, whether a parent link is required, and the solution ids whose records are still to be written.
inputs: A folder of the five record files, the parsed template, and optionally the ids of the overall network.
outputs: A list of problem lines, each starting with its rule id.
usage_notes: Runs inside the full check as rule S26, or alone as the records command.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A record is complete and linked or it is not; the cases pin what the check must keep.

name: Python template reader
scoped_purpose: Use for reading the intent template from the skill's SKILL.md into a field list, and for generating the non-code templates and excerpts from it. Avoids adding fields of its own or interpreting the template.
goals: The field list equals the template's fields after every refinement, and a refinement never renames a field whose words still identify it.
knowledge: The template's layout in SKILL.md; the stable keys for bare questions.
measures_of_success: A refinement shows up as named missing fields on the next check, with no hand edit of any schema.
parameters: The path to the source file, and whether to only compare.
outputs: The parsed field list, the per-type templates, the record headers and the verbatim excerpts.
effects: Writes the generated files; fails the check when the committed field list is stale.
usage_notes: Run the sync after the template's author edits it; a repository that cannot read the source uses the committed copy.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A field is read the same way or it is not; the cases pin the reading rules.

name: Python ownership rules
scoped_purpose: Use for assigning every file to exactly one component and checking layers, size and docstrings. Avoids describing what the code does.
goals: No file unowned, no module past the size ceiling, imports pointing inward.
measures_of_success: Code that serves no solution is found and removed.
parameters: Layer order, size ceiling, the layers that may not read the environment.
inputs: The file list and the component records.
outputs: Problem lines for rules S1 to S6 and S13.
usage_notes: A new file joins a component in the same change.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A file has one owner and an import points inward or it does not.

name: Python selector
scoped_purpose: Use for choosing which implementation serves a swappable solution by name, override or table default. Avoids deciding which one is best.
goals: Switching is a data change; an unknown name fails with the choices; targets load lazily.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone and no typo falls back silently.
inputs: A selection table of module:Attribute targets.
outputs: The chosen class or factory, and its config class.
usage_notes: Keep the table default equal to the measured winner or a declared tie.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A name resolves as specified or it does not.

name: Python harness
scoped_purpose: Use for running one implementation over a component's cases and recording the result with its provenance. Avoids ranking.
goals: Every recorded result carries its commit, case hash, cost and tokens; a call budget stops a run.
knowledge: Evaluation practice for models: held-out cases, staged sample sizes.
measures_of_success: Any result can be rerun from its record.
parameters: Component, implementation, case subset, sample size, call budget.
inputs: Case files, an implementation module with a build function.
usage_notes: Start small and stop at the budget; re-record on committed code.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A record carries its provenance and a budget is enforced, or it does not.

name: Python leaderboard
scoped_purpose: Use for deciding, from recorded results, which implementation is best or whether they tie. Avoids running anything.
goals: A win only outside the noise margin; ties, losses and unmeasured arms are labelled.
knowledge: Noise in small judged samples; cost accounting.
measures_of_success: Its verdicts match known rankings on pinned cases.
parameters: Noise margin and spend tolerance per component.
inputs: The results log and the registry.
outputs: A verdict per solution and a ranked board.
usage_notes: The check requires the selected implementation to be the winner or a declared tie.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A verdict is right for a result set or it is not.

name: Python check runner
scoped_purpose: Use for running every structural rule over a repository on each change. Avoids judging code quality beyond the rules.
goals: Every rule violation is reported by rule and path; a clean tree passes; strict mode refuses results from uncommitted code.
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is caught and nothing clean is flagged.
parameters: Strict mode, rules disabled, plugin rules.
inputs: The repository, its records, its results log, its waivers.
outputs: A list of violations and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A violation is reported by the right rule or it is not.

name: Python tracker
scoped_purpose: Use for building the review sheet tabs from the records and results, and syncing them with a spreadsheet. Avoids being a second source of truth.
goals: Every record and its latest verdict is in the tabs; reviewers' notes survive rebuilds.
knowledge: Spreadsheets as the review medium; row-keyed two-way merge.
measures_of_success: A reviewer can make and record every review decision from the sheet.
parameters: Extra columns per tab, the sheet id and credentials.
inputs: The registry and the results log.
outputs: Tracker tab files and the synced sheet.
usage_notes: Rebuild after any registry or result change.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A tab follows the registry and keeps reviewers' notes or it does not.

name: Python consumer check
scoped_purpose: Use for letting a repository that builds on a library record which library solution each integration serves and see its pin lag. Avoids copying the library's checks.
goals: Every integration point maps to a library solution and has a current result; the pin's lag is visible.
measures_of_success: The consumer passes with nothing unmapped or unexplained.
parameters: The consumer's registry, root, requirements, solutions and results; whether lag fails.
inputs: The consumer repository and the installed library.
usage_notes: Run in the consumer's tests; bump the pin after the library changes.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A drifted integration is caught or it is not.

name: Documentation and templates
scoped_purpose: Use for explaining ESOI and giving fill-in templates that need no code, so anyone can apply it by hand first. Avoids restating the author's template in other words.
goals: A newcomer can write an overall network and a first solution from the templates alone.
knowledge: The skill's definitions, principles and intent template, quoted.
measures_of_success: Someone following the guides alone reaches a passing check.
usage_notes: Read the explanation first, then copy a template.
invariant_reason: The documentation is one set with no rival implementation to rank.
gap: No recorded run measures how a newcomer fares with the documentation.
action: Have a newcomer follow the guides in a fresh repository and record the effort as a run.

name: This repository's metric run policy
scoped_purpose: Use for stating when this repository's own metrics are run, who approves, and when a result is stale. Avoids governing any other repository's metrics.
goals: Every metric here is offline and runs on every change; a recorded result is current only if it was run on committed code that has not changed since.
knowledge: The explanation in docs/explanation/when-metrics-are-run.md and this repository's filled policy in structure/metric-run-policy.md.
measures_of_success: The strict check passes on the default branch, and a stale result is found by the check rather than by a person.
parameters: Trigger: every change for the offline metrics, in the test suite and in continuous integration; a paid metric only when a decision depends on it, in staged samples inside a call budget and with Joshua's approval.
inputs: The committed code, the case files and the results log.
outputs: A row per run in the results log with the commit and the hash of the cases; the strict check's verdict.
effects: Offline metrics call no paid service and no network; a paid metric calls a model only when it is run on a decision. Re-recording changes only the results log.
usage_notes: After changing measured code or cases, commit, then run `esoi run --stale`, then commit the results.
invariant_reason: A result is called stale or current correctly, or it is not; the cases pin the rules.

name: Python skill distribution
scoped_purpose: Use for generating a public copy of a skill from a private folder, checking it for staleness and leaks, and installing it. Avoids hosting the copy and avoids judging the skill's content.
goals: The generated copy equals the source after every edit, a planted leak of each kind is always found, and an install never overwrites a different skill without being told.
knowledge: The include list and substitutions in the configuration; the private-span marker; the generic leak patterns.
measures_of_success: Every drift and leak case is caught by the right check, a clean copy passes, and each install case ends as the case says.
parameters: The source folder, the private term file, the install destination and whether to replace.
inputs: A skill folder and a configuration table that names only public things.
outputs: The copy folders, a list of problems with their kinds, and an installed folder.
effects: Writes the copies; fails the check on a stale copy or a leak; an install writes into a skills folder.
usage_notes: Run `esoi skill sync` and `esoi skill check` after the source changes; `esoi skill install` needs neither source nor configuration.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A copy is current and clean or it is not; the cases pin what the sync and the check must keep.

name: Behave by ESOI
scoped_purpose: Use for measuring, case by case, whether an AI agent's reply acts by the evolvable-structure principles, and for comparing the ways of giving an agent those principles. Avoids judging the quality of work in general and avoids rewording the principles (the author's skill is the authority).
goals: Every principle has cases, including cases of holding back and of keeping a qualifier; the recorded good replies pass and the recorded bad replies fail; every arm that calls a model is measured on the same cases and sample, inside an approved call budget.
knowledge: The author's skill, its principles and its nuance rules; the intent template; evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, a no-instructions baseline, staged samples).
measures_of_success: Offline: the recorded replies are classified as their authors meant and a keyword-stuffing baseline fails the restraint cases. Live: the skill arms pass more cases than no skill, with restraint cases passing as often as build cases.
parameters: The arm (standing instructions, on request, no skill), the model and judge model, the case subset (--sample, --only) and the call budget (--max-calls).
inputs: The rows of cases.csv, the bundled skill, and for a live arm a model command in ESOI_MODEL_COMMAND.
outputs: A reply per case, a pass or fail with a note, and a headline of passes per principle.
effects: A live arm calls a model and costs money; the offline arms call none.
usage_notes: Run reference_good and reference_bad on every change to the cases or esoi.behaviour. Run a live arm only on a decision and with approved spend (structure/metric-run-policy.md). Add a case when someone corrects an agent.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: the skill as standing instructions is how the author's skill is meant to be used, and the choice stands until a measured arm beats it
gap: The arms that call a model are not measured yet, so nothing shows how much the skill changes behaviour or which way of giving it is best.
action: Run the staged sample for each arm once Joshua approves the spend, then adopt the measured winner or declare a tie.

name: Judge ESOI behaviour
scoped_purpose: Use for grading one reply against one case when the patterns cannot tell, and for measuring how far that grading agrees with labelled replies. Avoids scoring behaviour itself (behave-by-esoi does that, with this judge's help) and avoids grading general quality.
goals: A judge is scored on a labelled good and bad reply for every case; false passes and false fails are counted apart; the share of labels that are a person's is visible; the judge prompt carries the rubric in words and never the patterns or the recorded replies.
knowledge: Practice for model judges (agreement with human labels, preference for its own phrasing, bias); the case rubric; the author's verdicts as the authority.
measures_of_success: A judge agrees with the labels on good and bad replies alike, a judge that passes everything is caught, and agreement is reported against a person's verdicts once they exist.
parameters: The judge model, the labelled replies and the human verdict column.
inputs: A behaviour case and one recorded reply.
outputs: A verdict and a reason, scored against the label.
effects: The model judge calls a model per reply, which costs money; the regex judge calls none.
usage_notes: Fill human_verdict in cases.csv to move the labels from the case author's to a person's. Regenerate cases.csv with write_cases when the behaviour cases change; a test fails until the two match.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: the model judge is the only arm that can credit a reply that acts well in other words, and it is used only with its agreement shown
gap: The model judge is not measured yet and every label is still the case author's, so agreement cannot show calibration against a person.
action: Have a person fill human_verdict for a sample of replies, then run the judge on a staged sample once Joshua approves the spend.
